attacks.claim: The rollback path does not carry Ghost-side unsubscribes, bounces, and complaints back to MailPoet. Re-enabling MailPoet sending after a 30-day window could re-mail readers who opted out, and sent email cannot be recalled.
attacks.evidence: "rollback = repoint DNS and re-enable MailPoet sending, with any new Ghost signups exported and re-imported to MailPoet"; ABSENT: any step that syncs Ghost suppressions back to MailPoet before sends resume

attacks.claim: Rollback can produce dual-sending and divergent state. Both Ghost and MailPoet are live during the 30-day window, and the plan has no double-send prevention and no rule for which system is authoritative for member and paid-subscription changes.
attacks.evidence: "rollback = repoint DNS and re-enable MailPoet sending"; ABSENT: double-send guard, or a rule for reconciling member and subscription changes made after cutover

attacks.claim: The whole send pipeline, database, and backups run on one 4 vCPU / 8 GB VPS with no redundancy and no documented load test at 46k recipients. This repeats the single-box failure mode behind the four send-day outages the plan is meant to fix.
attacks.evidence: "self-hosted via the official Docker image on a new 4 vCPU / 8 GB VPS ... MySQL 8 on the same box"; ABSENT: capacity test or failover plan

attacks.claim: No handling is specified for a bulk send that crashes or stalls partway through. The plan does not say how a resume avoids double-mailing or skipping recipients, or how a stalled send is detected.
attacks.evidence: "Bulk newsletter delivery: Ghost uses Mailgun for bulk email"; ABSENT: retry, resume, idempotency, or stall-detection behaviour

attacks.claim: The seed-send gate auto-releases the remaining ~44k recipients after 2 hours based on bounce and complaint rates. Mailgun events are asynchronous and can lag, so the gate can pass on incomplete data. No named owner holds a manual hold or abort decision, and the plan does not say what happens if metrics are not yet available at the 2-hour mark.
attacks.evidence: "the remainder sends 2 hours later if bounce rate < 2% and complaint rate < 0.1%"; ABSENT: metric owner, manual hold, abort procedure, or behaviour when metrics are missing

attacks.claim: Paid membership and Stripe are dual-running. Ghost is connected to the same Stripe account while the old membership and Stripe plugins remain for 30 days, so renewals, cancellations, and failed payments can be handled by both. No rule says which system is authoritative, and no step disables the old plugins at cutover.
attacks.evidence: "Stripe: existing Stripe account connected directly; no change in processor" and "WordPress stays running read-only on the old VPS for 30 days"; ABSENT: disabling old plugins at cutover, or a reconciliation rule for subscription events

attacks.claim: The 46k-recipient list is sent from a Mailgun domain warmed for about two weeks, with no volume ramp, no reputation-failure fallback, and the old MailPoet sender retired at cutover. This is a deliverability risk for the first real send, and sender reputation damage is hard to reverse.
attacks.evidence: "Mailgun domain warm-up (SPF/DKIM/DMARC)" in week 2; "Week 4: cutover Tuesday, seeded first send Thursday"; ABSENT: warm-up volume schedule or fallback sender

attacks.claim: Backups are untested at the point that matters. Nightly dumps allow up to about 24 hours of data loss. The only restore test is a JSON export round-trip into a scratch instance, not a full MySQL restore to a fresh host, and no alert covers a failed backup or export job.
attacks.evidence: "nightly encrypted dumps to object storage (30-day retention)"; "we restore one export into a scratch Ghost instance in week 2"; ABSENT: MySQL restore drill, measured recovery time, backup-failure alerting

attacks.claim: No observability or alerting is designed. Uptime, send-job health, queue depth, Mailgun failures, Stripe webhook failures, and disk and database health are all unspecified, even though send-day outages are the stated motivation.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: monitoring, alerting, or on-call plan; the only send-day measure is "Zero send-day outages over the first quarter"

attacks.claim: Scope and capacity are not realistic. A 0.5 FTE developer plus a managing editor must run VPS build, theme port, 2,000-URL redirects, Stripe migration, 37 manual reconciliations, and editor training, plus ongoing Docker, MySQL, and Ghost patching. The plan has no contingency and only 2 days of buffer before the first Ghost send.
attacks.evidence: "Owner: dev (0.5 FTE) + managing editor | 4 weeks"; "giving 2 days to fix issues before the first Ghost send"

attacks.claim: Suppression honouring is asserted but not verified before the first real send. The plan imports opt-outs as suppressed but has no step confirming Ghost excludes them from the 46k send.
attacks.evidence: "Unsubscribed and bounced addresses are imported as suppressed (never as active), so nobody who opted out is re-mailed."; ABSENT: pre-send check that suppressed addresses are excluded

attacks.claim: Personal data flows to Mailgun, Postmark, and object storage with no stated data processing agreements, transfer assessment, or sub-processor review.
attacks.evidence: "Mailgun only receives per-send recipient batches"; "Postmark Broadcasts"; "nightly encrypted dumps to object storage"; ABSENT: DPAs or sub-processor review

attacks.claim: Production subscriber and consent data is copied to staging and a scratch instance with no stated access controls, retention limit, or deletion step.
attacks.evidence: "Dry-run import on staging in week 1"; "restore one export into a scratch Ghost instance in week 2"

attacks.claim: Backups keep deleted or unsubscribed-and-deleted members for up to 30 days, and the plan does not address erasure timing.
attacks.evidence: "nightly encrypted dumps to object storage (30-day retention)"

attacks.claim: The weekly members CSV export is a full copy of the subscriber list. The plan does not state that it is encrypted, only that it is stored with the DB dumps.
attacks.evidence: "Ghost's members CSV export and JSON content export are scheduled weekly (cron, stored with the DB dumps)"

attacks.claim: Consent IP addresses are imported with no stated purpose or retention decision, which widens exposure of personal data.
attacks.evidence: "consent source/IP where recorded"

attacks.claim: No retention, archival, or deletion step is defined for MailPoet consent records or the old WordPress database after the 30-day read-only period.
attacks.evidence: "WordPress stays running read-only on the old VPS for 30 days"; ABSENT: post-day-30 retention or deletion step for consent evidence

attacks.claim: The 37 manual email reconciliations involve personal data, but the plan does not say who handles them or how the changes are logged.
attacks.evidence: "37 members with mismatched emails ... will be resolved by hand before cutover"

attacks.claim: Costs for the 30-day parallel run, the Postmark rehearsal, and backup storage at 30-day retention are not budgeted. The $140/mo figure is steady-state only.
attacks.evidence: "Total run cost: ~$140/mo VPS + Mailgun + storage, vs $95/mo today."; "WordPress stays running read-only on the old VPS for 30 days"

attacks.claim: The Mailgun $90/mo figure has no stated pricing tier or per-email rate. It is unverified against roughly 198k emails per month, and seed, re-send, and transactional volume are not counted.
attacks.evidence: "Estimated $90/mo at our volume (46k x ~4.3 sends/month)."
